- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots the next period; cap forecast increase at 3–5% above prior peak.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in adjusting downward; apply 1–2 day lag correction to downward moves.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price moving back toward 70–72 range), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 10–15%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 18 days.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.67/0.33), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.
